newsitem.title: FRANCE: France will not extend car rebate scheme.
newsitem.headline: France will not extend car rebate scheme.

text.p: The French government will not extend a new-cars-for-old rebate programme beyond its scheduled expiry on September 30, an industry ministry spokesman said.
"The car rebates will not be extended. It was decided today," the spokesman told Reuters.
He said he could not say if any other measures would be introduced to help the car industry.
The year-long programme has buoyed French car sales, which were up 7.4 percent in the first eight months of the 1996.
Sales were up 29.4 percent in July and industry sources expect a surge this month of around 70 percent as buyers rush to take advantage of the programme before it ends.
Industry Minister Franck Borotra recently defended the scheme, but Finance Minister Jean Arthuis was reported to be opposed to any extension.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe sounded in recent remarks as if he were not inclined to favour an extension. He said the scheme appeared to have helped foreign carmakers more than it did the French.
The French carmakers are split on the issue.
PSA Peugeot Citroen has asked the government for continued support, either in the form of rebates proportional to car prices or through a cut in the value-added tax on cars.

Renault SA, which formally entered the private sector in July, said it was not asking for an extension of the rebates or any other special assistance. On Wednesday it announced plans to cut prices as part of a more aggressive marketing policy.
The rebates, nicknamed "Juppettes" after the prime minister, were introduced a year ago to shore up the market which was crumbling after the expiry of a previous 17-month rebate scheme.
Although the car companies were grateful for the support, they said the rebates tended to skew sales toward cheaper models with thinner profit margins.
